pointblank started as an R package
(see [Data validation: R (pointblank)](0720-data-validation-r-pointblank.qmd)),
and has been ported to Python:
<https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/>

In this chapter we validate the Palmer penguins data,
which records measurements of 344 penguins from three islands in Antarctica.

```{python}
import pointblank as pb  # needs pointblank 1.3.0 or later, for get_row_flags()
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins
```

## Where are the missing values?

Before we write any rules,
it helps to know where the data is missing.
`pb.missing_vals_tbl()` shows the missing values in each column,
split into sections of rows from the top of the data to the bottom:

```{python}
pb.missing_vals_tbl(data=penguins)
```

## Checking values

We validate the data in two parts.
The first part checks that the values we do have are sensible,
and the second part, in the next section, checks for missing values.
Keeping them apart makes each report easier to read,
because a value outside its range and a value that is missing
are different problems that we usually handle in different ways.

A validation starts with `pb.Validate()`,
which takes the data and, optionally, a label for the report.
Each validation step we chain onto it is one rule,
and `interrogate()` runs every step:

```{python}
values = (
    pb.Validate(
        data=penguins,
        label="Penguin measurements",
        thresholds=(0.01, 0.05, 0.10),  # warning, error, critical
    )
    .col_vals_in_set(columns="species", set=["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"])
    .col_vals_between(columns="bill_length_mm", left=30, right=60, na_pass=True)
    .col_vals_between(columns="body_mass_g", left=3000, right=5500, na_pass=True)
    .col_vals_ge(columns="flipper_length_mm", value=185, na_pass=True)
    .rows_distinct()
    .interrogate()
)
values
```

Setting `na_pass=True` lets missing values pass a step,
so these steps only judge the values that are there.

The `thresholds` set how much failure we tolerate before pointblank raises a flag.
A step is marked with a warning when at least 1% of its rows fail,
an error at 5%,
and critical at 10%.
The report shows which level each step reached.

Each row of the report is one step.
To see which penguins failed a step,
we ask for that step's report by its number:

```{python}
values.get_step_report(i=3)  # which penguins failed step 3?
```

## Checking missing values

The second validation checks for missing values.
`col_vals_not_null()` checks that a column has no missing values,
and `rows_complete()` checks that no row has a missing value in any column:

```{python}
missing = (
    pb.Validate(
        data=penguins,
        label="Penguin missing values",
        thresholds=(0.01, 0.05, 0.10),  # warning, error, critical
    )
    .col_vals_not_null(columns=["bill_length_mm", "sex"])
    .rows_complete()
    .interrogate()
)
missing
```

Giving `col_vals_not_null()` two columns creates one step for each column,
so this validation has three steps.
The thresholds turn these checks into a rule about how much missingness we accept,
which is the "missingness not beyond expected threshold" item
from the checklist in [Data validation](0710-data-validation.qmd).

## Splitting the passing and failing rows

After interrogating a validation,
we can split the data into the rows that passed every step
and the rows that failed at least one.
We keep working with the rows that passed,
and give the rows that failed to a teammate to fix:

```{python}
passed = values.get_sundered_data(type="pass")  # keep working with these
failed = values.get_sundered_data(type="fail")  # a teammate fixes these
pb.preview(data=failed)  # a quick look at the rows that failed
```

```{python}
failed.to_csv("penguins_to_fix.csv", index=False)
```

Because our value checks use `na_pass=True`,
a row with missing values can still be in `passed`.
Whether to drop or keep those rows is a decision for the missing values validation.

## Flagging every row

`get_row_flags()` returns every row of the data,
with a column for each step that is `True` where the row failed that step,
the number of steps the row failed,
and the fraction of steps it passed:

```{python}
values.get_row_flags()  # every row, with the checks it failed
```
